title: Backers of U.S. Film Incentive See Window to Pass Bill This Year
description: Supporters of a federal film incentive are preparing an all-out push to pass the legislation by the end of the year, looking to take advantage of mo
body:
Supporters of a federal film incentive are preparing an all-out push to pass the legislation by the end of the year, looking to take advantage of momentum before Congress potentially changes hands next term.

	A bipartisan group of senators and representatives unveiled the bill on Thursday. It would provide a 20%-30% federal incentive for films and TV shows that would stack on top of state incentives, instantly making states like California, Georgia and New York among the world’s most generous film locations.
	

	“Windows of opportunity to pass legislation open and close very quickly,” said Rep. Linda Sanchez, D-Calif., at a press conference on Thursday. “You have to really strike while the iron is hot.”


	The House of Representatives is out of session, and will not return until after the November election. But lawmakers expect that the lame-duck session will include a significant tax bill, into which the U.S. film incentive could be incorporated.

	“It is the goal and it is realistic,” said Nathaniel Moran, R-Texas, in an interview. “When the right opportunity strikes, you’ve gotta jump at the opportunity. The stars have aligned where we have bicameral, bipartisan support, and we have a president who is very supportive of this.”

	The bill introduced on Thursday has yet to get a cost estimate. As proposed, the incentive would cover a wide range of productions, including animation and reality shows. It would also cover salaries for actors and other above-the-line talent. A separate visual effects and postproduction credit would also apply to projects that are filmed abroad but completed domestically.

	Asked whether the bill is a starting point for negotiations, or whether it may pass in something close to its current form, Moran said that time will tell.

	“There is a long way to go,” he said. “One of the things that’s important is to get a score on the bill, to look for pay-fors that might offset any cost associated with the bill … Whether or not it changes a little bit or a lot will be determined by the feedback we get.”

	The proposal includes a benefit for rural areas like Moran’s district — a 5% bonus for rural “opportunity zones” — as well as something for Los Angeles, in the form of a 5% bonus for filming in a federal disaster zone. (Due to last year’s fires, L.A. County qualifies through January 2030.)
	

	“It was important for me to have that in there,” said Rep. Laura Friedman, D-Calif. “Film is very unique in terms of its ability to stand up a lot of jobs quickly.”

	As written, the credit would stack on top of state-based incentives — with no reduction in qualified spend due to state credits — which would push the total subsidy into the 50% range in several states.

	“The state tax incentives are separate and apart from the tax incentives here,” Moran said. “We see this as an additional incentive for the companies to benefit from to stay here.”

	Sen. Adam Schiff, a Democratic sponsor of the bill, said he is eager to get it done this year, rather than let the momentum flag.

	“The iron is very hot right now,” he said. “We’re all very focused on this, the president is focused on this. I wouldn’t want to see that bleed into next year.”

	Still, Friedman cautioned, it’s not a sure thing.

	“There’s a lot that has to happen for that to be a reality,” she said.

schema.headline: Backers of U.S. Film Incentive See Window to Pass Bill This Year

title: ‘The Musical’ Star Will Brill on His Dark, Surprisingly Delightful 9/11 Revenge Comedy
description:
“You rarely see a movie now where the big question is, ‘How the fuck did this get made? Who let them do this?'”

	Tony award winner WIll Brill asks
body:
“You rarely see a movie now where the big question is, ‘How the fuck did this get made? Who let them do this?'”

	Tony award winner WIll Brill asks this aloud over a meal with Variety at West Hollywood’s Canter’s Deli. Brill starts with a steaming bowl of soup at 11 a.m. before joyfully moving on to French toast. The Broadway vet is rail thin, but as hungry for diner classics as he is to discuss “The Musical” — his darkly comic Sundance gem that’s now rolling out in limited theatrical release. 
	

	Brill plays the nebbish Doug, a middle school theater teacher smitten with his colleague Abigail. When he learns that his beloved has taken up with the school’s principal — a smug “Chad” played expertly by Rob Lowe — Doug sets off on an absurd revenge quest. Lowe’s principal is out for a blue ribbon prize from the school district, and to sabotage his ambitions Doug stages an original musical in secret starring his earnest, talented young students. The titular musical is a recounting of the 9/11 terror attacks, with original music and cardboard Twin Towers ablaze.  


	While audacious and almost surely offensive, Brill and his director Giselle Bonilla pull off the impossible: a broadly comic look at obsession and bitterness, laced with a healthy dose of sunshine thanks to its innocent cast of kids. Here, he discusses revenge, risky cinema and the jokes left on the cutting room floor. 

	I understand you have a deep connection to student theater.

	Will Brill: What’s cool in a holistic sense about this movie, is that I came from doing children’s theater. I started when I was six years old. I was in “The Velveteen Rabbit.” I remember distinctly the auditions and the chaos and the friendships built — and the gunning for the same roles and never getting them. Some kids were always ahead of you. What’s so funny about this movie is [my character] is the one experiencing the petty highs and lows, and he’s the adult in the room. A lot of my comedy specifically comes from never getting cast as the leading man in anything. I was always the kid playing the old man or having to do funny voices. I was the badger in “The Wind and the Willows” and the king in “Cinderella.”
	

	Why do you think those were the parts you got?

	They put me in those roles because I was so obsessed with Robin Williams and Jim Carrey and was trying to emulate those guys. And still! When Robin died, I couldn’t — I still haven’t really watched his movies because I think of him as a part of who I am.

	This film is about revenge, which is one of the more human tendencies to make a movie about.

	Anybody can identify with having lost a person with whom they were infatuated, or a job that they thought was going to change the course of their life. We did a marketing push for this movie where we asked strangers, “What is the pettiest thing you’ve ever done?” It helped me remember that in my sophomore year of college, there was this girl I had an ongoing flirtation with, but she wanted to keep it secret. Another guy was love with her. We come back from break and she’s dating this other guy. She asked me how my summer was, and I just said, “Oh, I started dating someone. I have a girlfriend back at home.”

	Which directly mirrors the plot of this movie. You were lying when you said that?

	It was a lie! I pulled the name of a close friend of mine at home. And it makes me think — my character in “The Musical,” Doug, is so obviously a villain. There are people who will watch this movie and say, “I can’t get behind this because he’s so wretched, and because what he’s doing is so bad.” But I think most people will realize, “He’s doing the thing that all of us have fantasized about, and none of us have the cojones to do.”

	They should come work in Hollywood for a day.

	That’s a good point. Doug wants a kind of [creative success], but he wouldn’t last a day here. He’d never survive what most of us have been through in this industry.

	It was a creative risk, incorporating 9/11 so heavily into this story, especially involving a kids theater troupe. It illustrates how far you character is willing to go to embarrass his nemesis. Were you ever nervous about how it would play?

	[Our screenwriter] Alex Heller and I were talking about this last night. I was obsessed with the character from the start, and Alex said he watched the original “The Producers” and “Election” when writing this. After, he just wrote in his notes app, “Fuck it: 9/11 musical.” It’s so funny because it’s a really insane thing to do. It’s so callous and despicable. What’s interesting is that some of our kid actors had done plays about 9/11 in school. But this movie [takes a shot] at everyone. You see the snowflake liberal school administration people get so overwhelmed about anything off color. But something about putting that concept for a musical in the hands of children defangs it. The musical’s audience in the film are all horrified, but you also see them gasp and crack up because the kids are so winning.
	

	You’ve done a lot of Broadway and a lot of drama. Was it hard to lobby for such a broad comedic part?

	Well, the proof of concept for this film starred an Instagram-famous performer. My first question to [director] Giselle Bonilla was, “Why didn’t you hire that guy?” She told me it was the same reason she’d offered the role to Andrew Garfield and Adam Driver before me. It’s the person [behind the character]. They initially offered me [Rob Lowe’s part of] the principal.

	Once again, they cast you as the old man in the play.

	There was a cycle of actors this went through before [I got the lead] and Gillian Jacobs was cast. 10 days before we started shooting, the previous leads dropped out. Coincidentally, our producer had a meeting with Rob Lowe and gave him the script and he was obsessed. Especially when he found out we were filming in L.A. He felt it was the kind of comedy he’d been dying to see for ages. You rarely see a movie now where the big question is, “How the fuck did this get made? Who let them do this?”

	Rob is incredible in this film. The most smug – you describe him as a “Chad.”

	My girlfriend and I were just talking about the people you meet in your life who are really performatively sincere. Typically, about veganism or human rights. She relayed this story to me about Cristin Milioti being at a table read. She was eating a hardboiled egg and one of her costars asked her, “Do you consider yourself a feminist?” And she said, “Uh, yeah.” He was like, “So you don’t have a problem eating female animals?”

	Stop.

	But Rob was incredible. He’s such a good improviser. There was a line they cut, when he sees the musical for the first time, it was: “You turned the gymnasium into Ground Zero. Are you fucking mental?” There was also another point where he said, “My brother was a first responder … in Burbank.”

	You had a really strong premiere at Sundance, but it took a minute for a deal to get done to release this movie. I heard distributors were nervous about this.

	I have definitely come to the to a reconciliation that my taste is not everyone’s taste, and my taste is especially not corporate America’s taste. I was listening to Andy Richter talking about the corporatization of the entertainment industry, and he’s so right. Nobody is able to go out and take chances anymore because people don’t want to support that. Rob has a list that he goes through of stuff that he can’t believe people funded. One of the OG’s is “The Book of Mormon.” You watch that and you’re like, “This is so inflammatory. This is so crazy.” You can say that they’re punching down, and there’s a whole talk that we can have about like the Church of Latter Day Saints and what they’ve earned and what they haven’t. But there is also there is also an element of love in that play for Mormons, which is really cool.

schema.headline: ‘The Musical’ Star Will Brill on His Dark, Surprisingly Delightful 9/11 Revenge Comedy

title: Tamera Mowry-Housley Joins ‘Scrubs’ Reboot Season 2
description:
Tamera Mowry-Housley is checking into Season 2 of the “Scrubs” reboot.

	The “Sister, Sister” and “Twitches” star has boarded the ABC sitcom as a gu
body:
Tamera Mowry-Housley is checking into Season 2 of the “Scrubs” reboot.

	The “Sister, Sister” and “Twitches” star has boarded the ABC sitcom as a guest star. She will play Dr. Steffie, a pediatric doctor who tries to persuade Tosh (Ava Bunn) to choose peds as her specialty. Season 2 premieres with two episodes on Wednesday, Sept. 30, at 8 p.m. on ABC. Episodes stream on Hulu and Disney+ the next day.


	Mowry-Housley joins the 30-minute revival comedy alongside Zach Braff as John “J.D.” Dorian, Donald Faison as Christopher Turk, Sarah Chalke as Elliot Reid and Ava Bunn as Sam Tosh.
	

	The second iteration of the series finds J.D., Turk and Elliot after they’ve leveled up from interns to icons at Sacred Heart. Per the logline, “Now, the respected doctors inspire the next generation while balancing the ups and downs of working in a hospital. Together with characters new and old, they are navigating this next chapter with laughter, heart and some surprises along the way.”

	Bill Lawrence of Doozer Productions created the original series and serves as executive producer of the reboot alongside Jeff Ingold and Liza Katzer also of Doozer Productions. Braff, Faison and Chalke star and executive produce. Aseem Batra serves as executive producer and showrunner; Mike Royce, Mathew Harawitz, Randall Keenan Winston and Michael Spiller also executive produce. The series is produced by 20th Television, a part of Disney Television Studios.

	The original “Scrubs” premiered in 2001 and ran for nine seasons on NBC and then ABC.

title: Xsolla President’s New Book Reveals How Gaming Companies Can ‘Get Off That Hit-Driven Hamster Wheel’
description: Amid more layoffs and contraction and renewed going-discless discourse, we are facing no shortage of opinions about what strategies will finally rig
body:
Amid more layoffs and contraction and renewed going-discless discourse, we are facing no shortage of opinions about what strategies will finally rightsize the global-gaming-industry ship. Apart from relying on the highly anticipated release of “Grand Theft Auto VI” to solve for the nearly $350 billion industry’s problems, a new book by Xsolla president Chris Hewish has a few clear suggestions.

	Titled “Durable Advantage: Five Pillars of the Modern Game Business,” the book debuted last month at Gamescom 2026 in Cologne, the annual meeting of the minds for the bigwigs in the gaming industry. In the text, Hewish outlines a handful of areas that, when utilized to the fullest, make up a healthy gaming business: relationships, commerce, intelligence, trust and time.
	

	“Not just great games, but they’ve really built up this business around these five framework pillars,” Hewish tells Variety. “They are governing those pillars when it comes to their business. They’re not completely reliant completely on somebody else for all of those. So the direct analogy is companies that are only working through platforms like the app stores are completely reliant on them for the relationships with their players, for the commerce, for the business, behavioral intelligence on the players and it can slow down building trust with the players because of all of that.”

	As current president of a fintech company that makes payment software for video games, including its PayStation payment-integration tools and former exec at Activision and DreamWorks, Hewish wants those in the gaming industry to examine their first-party vs. third-party models and ask, “Are they actually owners or are they just renters of all of the different parts of their business?”
	

	When considering the “intelligence” pillar, Hewish says the gaming industry can “get off that hit-driven hamster wheel of always just being reliant on the next big hit” by taking a deeper look at more-informed data. This also requires looking for gaps in intelligence created when a company doesn’t have proprietary numbers for all aspects of its business, including monetization.

	“Companies all have dashboards,” Hewish says. “They know the number of active users. They know the revenue from those users. They know the revenue per user in a particular country. But right now, if they’re only looking at a dashboard, they haven’t really governed all of the intelligence of the data because if you put everything through another platform, the payment data, the commerce data, it stays with the platform, it doesn’t come through.”

	An example Hewish offers is a company noticing revenue dropping in one country and making incorrect assumptions based on its own incomplete data.

	“You may assume, oh my gosh, we need to make more content for that country because it’s just not relevant or we need to localize more in that country,” Hewish says. “And so you spend resources in that direction. The intelligence pillar is saying, well, hold on, you need a complete picture of what’s happening because what you have missed is the fact that there was a new payment method that was introduced in that country and it blew up. Like, Venmo came on the scene and 20% of your players have moved over to that new payment method, but your platform has not integrated it. So they literally have stopped using their old payment methods. They can’t use the new ones, so you see a drop in revenue and you erroneously think it’s a content problem and spend resources on that content.”

schema.headline: Xsolla President’s New Book Reveals How Gaming Companies Can ‘Get Off That Hit-Driven Hamster Wheel’

title: Letterboxd Suitors Include A24 and New York Times; Sale Could Value Social Movie Platform at $300 Million: Report
description: A bidding war may be in full flower for Letterboxd, the popular film-reviews and social service that has been fielding inbound acquisition offers fo
body:
A bidding war may be in full flower for Letterboxd, the popular film-reviews and social service that has been fielding inbound acquisition offers for several months.

	Indie studio A24 and the New York Times are the latest to express an interest in buying Letterboxd, according to a New York Times report citing anonymous sources. Any deal is “expected to value Letterboxd at more than $300 million,” per the report. That would be about 20 times its projected earnings in 2026 of roughly $15 million, according to the Times.
	

	There’s been broad interest in Letterboxd: Those said to have explored a possible acquisition include Netflix, Sony Pictures Entertainment, Paramount Skydance, private-equity giant TPG and Reddit co-creator Alexis Ohanian.


	Asked for comment, Katie Hill, the New York Times’ SVP, global head of communications and external affairs, said, “The company regularly reviews potential investments, and it’s our policy not to comment on speculation about potential acquisitions or divestitures.”

	A24 declined to comment. Reps for Letterboxd did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

	If a studio or streamer acquired Letterboxd, it would introduce at least the perception of a conflict of interest, as users might wonder if such an owner would favor its own titles on the service. Rotten Tomatoes was part of NBCUniversal for years, raising questions of its independence from the entertainment division. (Rotten Tomatoes is now part of Versant Media, which spun off from NBCU earlier this year.)

	In a statement in July, a Letterboxd spokesperson said about reports of potential buyers: “As Letterboxd has grown, it’s natural there will be interest in what we do next. There’s nothing specific for us to share at this time. Any decision about Letterboxd’s future would involve the founders.”
	

	Letterboxd, founded in 2011 and based in New Zealand, has been shopping itself to interested parties in recent months. It is majority-owned by Canadian holding company Tiny, which acquired a 60% stake in Letterboxd in 2023 at a valuation of $50 million-$60 million. Letterboxd co-founders Matthew Buchanan and Karl von Randow own the remaining 40% share.

	Letterboxd has more than 30 million members globally and serves a passionate base of movie lovers. The company also has launched an online video-rental service stocked with indie films including previously unreleased titles.

schema.headline: Letterboxd Suitors Include A24 and New York Times; Sale Could Value Social Movie Platform at $300 Million: Report

title: ‘Quiz From God’: Japanese Remake of CJ ENM K-Drama, Starring Mamiya Shotaro, Sets Global Prime Video Launch (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Mamiya Shotaro leads a Japanese remake of CJ ENM‘s Korean hit drama “Quiz From God,” which will stream exclusively on Prime Video from Dec. 4.

	The
body:
Mamiya Shotaro leads a Japanese remake of CJ ENM‘s Korean hit drama “Quiz From God,” which will stream exclusively on Prime Video from Dec. 4.

	The Prime Original series casts Mamiya as Hatsushima Haruto, a neurosurgeon turned forensic pathologist whose brilliance has earned him a reputation as a heaven-sent genius.

	Having quit neurosurgery for reasons that remain unexplained, Haruto now works at the National Forensic Autopsy Center, where he reads the clues the dead leave behind. The cases that land on his table are among Tokyo’s strangest: a divisive underground idol who dies during a performance, a young man who ends up dead after accepting illegal side work, and someone who dies without warning on a first date.
	

	Each investigation leads Haruto to uncommon diseases concealed behind deaths that at first seem to defy explanation, and to the social problems that sit beneath them.


	Haruto has a puzzle of his own to solve. He lives with a rare illness and never knows how much longer his body will hold up. A secret buried in his past could also turn everything on its head.

	The Korean original, fronted by Ryu Deok-hwan, was a major success at home and got viewers talking. It went on to run for five seasons. The Japanese version keeps the elements that made the original popular while giving the story a new setting, a different mood and its own point of view.

	Mamiya said his manager had first floated the idea of him starring in the drama more than a decade ago, when he was in his early 20s, prompting him to seek out the Korean series. “After many twists and turns, the project finally began moving forward last autumn, and before I knew it, we were already filming,” he said.
	

	“I’m especially happy that we were able to bring this project to life with the three producers, all of whom have known me well for many years,” Mamiya added. “This was my first time working with the director, but we were able to build a relationship of trust through our meetings, script readings, and filming. I hope you enjoy watching the drama.”

schema.headline: ‘Quiz From God’: Japanese Remake of CJ ENM K-Drama, Starring Mamiya Shotaro, Sets Global Prime Video Launch (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Serbia’s Screen Industries in Crisis Amid Claims That Blacklists, ‘State-Sponsored Censorship’ Are Designed to ‘Starve Independent Production’
description: The Serbian film and television industries are in a state of crisis, with independent production in the Balkan powerhouse crippled by what leading i
body:
The Serbian film and television industries are in a state of crisis, with independent production in the Balkan powerhouse crippled by what leading industry groups describe as “a coordinated campaign of state-sponsored censorship.”

	Nearly two years after a devastating train station disaster that killed 16 people and sparked mass demonstrations against the government of President Aleksandar Vučić, independent producers say they’re being shut out by state-aligned media and starved of financing by the national funding body, Film Center Serbia, which has not announced a public call in nearly two years.
	

	“There are virtually no independent sources of financing left in Serbia,” said one leading film and TV producer, who asked to remain anonymous for fear of potential repercussions. 


	“Whether you are looking for public funding for a film, financing from the national broadcaster, or investment from the other major media companies, all of the major sources of financing are now state-owned or state-controlled,” they added. “If you are considered politically undesirable, there is really nowhere else to go.”

	Earlier this year, a coalition of leading film guilds and professional associations issued a desperate plea to the international film community, alleging in an open letter that “political interference, informal blacklists of filmmakers and public attacks on artists have become systemic” in the once booming Balkan biz.

	“The Serbian film industry is currently facing a coordinated campaign of state-sponsored censorship,” read the letter, which was signed by eight industry bodies. “While Film Center Serbia continues to project a ‘business as usual’ image internationally, the reality is a total freeze on funding calls designed to starve independent production.”
	

	The tragedy at the Novi Sad railway station, where a concrete canopy collapsed in November 2024, killing 16 bystanders, sparked nationwide protests — among the largest in Europe in recent memory — and became a symbol of entrenched corruption in the Vučić administration. Prime Minister Miloš Vučević stepped down in the aftermath, though the president has rejected ongoing calls for his resignation.

	Director Jelena Maksimović, whose Venice-bound debut feature “Until the Day Ends” is set against the student protests that galvanized the nation, told Variety that “the attempt to silence us is part of a broader attack on workers, on collective organizing and on the possibility of imagining a society based on solidarity, equality and freedom.” 

	Producer Jelena Angelovski echoed her remarks, adding that “those who do not see eye to eye with the regime [are] thoroughly obstructed in their efforts to make films, regardless of whether or not these films are openly political.” 

	“For close to two years now all institutional funding for film production has been entirely suspended, except for those who are propagating the right-wing nationalist government’s corrupted ways,” she said. 

	The systematic silencing of opposition voices is part of what Angelovski describes as a broader strategy by the Vučić regime of “actively and by all possible means — from administrative to those involving physical violence and imprisonment — repressing all forms of opposition to its authoritarian and criminal methods of governance and its highly reactionary politics.”

	Critics accuse the country’s largest media groups, including the state-owned Telekom Srbija and the United Media conglomerate, of blacklisting creatives opposed to the right-wing government, what the veteran producer characterizes as “actors and filmmakers who are considered acceptable and those who are not.” 

	“Your public statements, your social media activity and whether you take part in protests can determine whether you get a role or a job,” they said.

	United Media did not respond to a request for comment. Aleksandra Martinović, chief multimedia and content officer at Telekom Srbija, rejected allegations of bias at the company and its production arm, TS Media, insisting the group is “completely open” to work with any and all talent, regardless of their political beliefs. 
	

	“Our results and our projects show what we are doing and the way we work,” she said. “We are completely open-minded.”

	Meanwhile, as the political deadlock shows no signs of resolution, Serbian industry professionals worry about the consequences that their silencing will have on society at large. 

	“This kind of censorship is leaving people without work and without a space for their voices to be heard,” said the veteran producer. “And when you systematically remove critical voices from film, television and the media, what you are left with is an increasingly dark and controlled public space.”

schema.headline: Serbia’s Screen Industries in Crisis Amid Claims That Blacklists, ‘State-Sponsored Censorship’ Are Designed to ‘Starve Independent Production’

title: ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ Adds 4 New Scenes Tying to ‘Doomsday’: [SPOILER] Fights Doctor Doom, [SPOILER] Travels to the Past and the Multiverse Collapses
description:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for “Avengers: Endgame Encore,” now playing in theaters.

	In the lead-up to “Avengers: Doomsday,” Mar
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for “Avengers: Endgame Encore,” now playing in theaters.

	In the lead-up to “Avengers: Doomsday,” Marvel has re-released “Avengers: Endgame” in theaters with four brand new scenes that tie directly into the sprawling team-up film releasing on Dec. 18. Retitled “Avengers: Endgame Encore,” this slightly longer version of the 2019 blockbuster adds four minutes of new footage with characters like Robert Downey Jr.’s mega-villain Doctor Doom, Tom Hiddleston’s Loki and Mark Ruffalo’s Bruce Banner to the already jam-packed movie.
	

	Marvel started building the hype for “Doomsday” a year ahead of its release with four short teasers attached to last year’s “Avatar: Fire and Ash.” The first revealed that Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) and Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell) have a son; the second focused on Thor (Chris Hemsworth) and his adopted daughter; the third showed Prof. Xavier (Patrick Stewart), Magneto (Ian McKellen) and Cyclops (James Marsden) from Fox’s “X-Men” universe crossing into the MCU; and the fourth brought together Black Panther (Letitia Wright) and the Wakandans with the Fantastic Four, who traveled from their universe.


	These new “Endgame Encore” scenes were shot during “Doomsday” production and added to the re-release to bridge the two massive “Avengers” stories. The first scene takes place during Steve and Peggy’s dance in the closing of “Endgame.” As fans saw in the original movie, Steve has hung up his Captain America costume, passed the star-spangled shield down to Sam Wilson (Anthony Mackie) and finally settled down with his long-lost love Peggy after traveling back in time. But now, they get a surprising knock at their door from none other than the Norse trickster god, Loki. The last time we saw the reformed villain was in the finale of “Loki” Season 2, where he resigned himself to holding up the entire multiverse for the rest of time. But before that, it seems that Loki, in his Time Variance Authority uniform, pays Steve and Peggy a visit, perhaps to discuss how they’ve created an unstable branch in the multiverse with Steve’s time travel. 
	

	“Loki” gets another look with a fellow scene that takes place in the Time Variance Authority with Mobius (Owen Wilson), Casey (Eugene Cordero), Ouroboros (Ke Huy Quan) and Miss Minutes (Tara Strong). They notice that two Earths are about to collide in an incursion and begin firing on each other. More alternate worlds start colliding and terminating, and it’s revealed that the entire multiverse is collapsing. Could those two Earths be Fox’s “X-Men” universe and the mainline MCU world? We already know that Prof. Xavier, Magneto, Cyclops, Mystique (Rebecca Romijn), Nightcrawler (Alan Cumming) and Gambit (Channing Tatum) will cross into the MCU, so this may set up their clash with the Avengers that was teased in the “Doomsday” trailer.

	Another new scene with Bruce Banner pops up during the credits and takes place after he’s apprehended in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” In this summer’s record-breaking blockbuster, Bruce loses control and is unable to stop from transforming into the Hulk when his mind is controlled by Jean Grey (Sadie Sink). Spider-Man (Tom Holland) beats the super-strong, green giant, and Bruce is taken to a secure medical facility. In the new “Endgame Encore” credits scene, Bruce is in an underground bunker tinkering on a serum to suppress his Hulking out. All of a sudden, Doctor Doom breaks into Bruce’s facility and Bruce turns into the roaring Hulk to face him, but we don’t see what happens next. Does this mean Bruce and/or Hulk will reappear in “Doomsday, and will he be under Doctor Doom’s control?

	The final new scene appears at the very end of the credits, when the original “Endgame” had a mysterious, metal-clanging sound in the closing moments. When “Endgame” first released, diehard fans realized that the noise was from “Iron Man” when Downey Jr. was forging his powerful suit of armor. Now, we see a flashes of Doctor Doom making his metal mask with the same sound being played. It’s a dark twist and seems to hint that Doom and Iron Man, while both played by Downey Jr., may also have their origins mirrored.

	“Avengers: Doomsday” hits theaters on Dec. 18 — the same day as “Dune: Part 3,” setting up a “Dunesday” showdown. With all of the new scenes, advance teasers and year-long countdown clock, Marvel and Disney are hoping “Doomsday” ends up being another smash hit in the wake of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s” record-setting run.

schema.headline: ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ Adds 4 New Scenes Tying to ‘Doomsday’: [SPOILER] Fights Doctor Doom, [SPOILER] Travels to the Past and the Multiverse Collapses

title: Jay Pharoah, Cheri Oteri, Adam Devine Among ‘Universal Basic Guys’ Season 3 Guest Stars (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Saturday Night Live” alums Jay Pharoah and Cheri Oteri, as well as “Workaholics” star Adam Devine, are among the guest stars set to appear on the u
body:
“Saturday Night Live” alums Jay Pharoah and Cheri Oteri, as well as “Workaholics” star Adam Devine, are among the guest stars set to appear on the upcoming Season 3 of Fox’s animated series “Universal Basic Guys.” 

	Also set to join in on the universal basic fun this season: Thomas Lennon (“Reno 911!”), Brandon Wardell (“Wonder Man”), David Alan Grier (“In Living Color”), Joe Lo Truglio (“Brooklyn Nine-Nine”) and William Stanford Davis (“Abbott Elementary”).
	

	The news was revealed Thursday at the SCAD Animation Fest in Atlanta, where “Universal Basic Guys” creators Adam Malamut and Craig Malamut teased the show’s Season 3 and screened the season premiere episode, “Rhoda.”

	On the show, which comes from Sony Pictures TV and Fox Entertainment, Pharoah will play “Hugh Truckner,” Oteri appears as “Renee,” Devine is “Chase Waters,” Lennon plays “Antoine Shmegmin,” Wardell shows up as “Darren,” Grier plays “Ferris,” Lo Truglio is “Bouchard” and Davis plays “Earl.”

	Pharoah’s credits also include “White Famous,” while Oteri is additionally known for “Scary Movie” and Devine is also known for “Pitch Perfect,” among other projects.  

	Additional guest voices this season include Brian George, Dana Snyder, Taylor Ortega, Matt Dusk, Chris Elliott, Carlos Alazraqui, Will Sasso, Jon Glaser, Echo Kellum, Kimberly Brooks, Krizia Bajos, Rachel Kaly, Eric Ladin, Rose Abdoo, Jimmi Simpson, Jessica McKenna, Leon Chen, Secunda Wood, Holmes, Eric Bauza, Brianna Gentilella, Tommy Pope, Susie Essman, Liam Cullagh, Will Angus, Anthony Gorgano, Jorge Garcia, Reid Scott, Rob Corddry, Ken Jeong, Retta, Michelle Ortiz, Joe Conklin, Danny Trejo, John Early, Lou Diamond Phillips, Yamaneika Saunders, André Sogliuzzo and Matt Dusk.
	



	

	



	Season 3 of “Universal Basic Guys” premieres Sunday, Sept. 27, at 9 p.m. ET on Fox, streaming on Hulu the next day. Adam Malamut and Craig Malamut are the creators and executive producers.

	“Universal Basic Guys” centers on two brothers, Mark and Hank Hoagies (both voiced by Adam Malamut), “who lose their jobs to automation and are given $3,000 a month in a new basic income program,” per the show’s logline. Now, they’re using their free time and free money to find purpose in a world where they’re no longer needed. This season, the Hoagies face their most chaotic chapter yet when the arrival of a new family member turns their lives upside down.”

	Besides Adam Malamut, the show also stars Talia Genevieve as Tammy Hoagies, Ally Maki (“Wrecked”) as Andrea and Fred Armisen (“Saturday Night Live,” “Portlandia”) as David.

	Fox Entertainment, via its animation studio Bento Box Entertainment, and Sony Pictures Television are the production companies behind the show. Besides Adam Malamut and Craig Malamut as co-creators and executive producers, Shane Kosakowski is also an executive producer.

	Jennifer Hudson, Pearlena Igbokwe, Melissa McCarthy and Sharon Stone were honored at the event, hosted by comedian Iliza Shlesinger. title: Chadwick Boseman's Widow Blasts His Brothers' Lawsuit As 'Smear' Campaign
description:
Chadwick Boseman's Widow
                          His Brothers Suing Me Over Estate is PR Stunt!
body:
Chadwick Boseman's Widow
                          His Brothers Suing Me Over Estate is PR Stunt!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 24, 2026
                            3:44 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Chadwick Boseman's widow is blasting his brothers for dragging her name through the mud ... claiming their lawsuit is nothing but a "public-relations stunt" to smear her in the tabloids.
      
    
            Taylor Simone Ledward filed a legal response, firing back at Derrick and Kevin Boseman, who recently asked the court to ax her as the administrator of the estate and replace her with attorney Jason Rubin.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Taylor says she shouldn't be removed from the position ... because she's done nothing wrong -- listing her numerous disbursements to Chadwick's parents, Carolyn and Leroy, in the years since his death.
      

            Page Six was the first to report on this news.
      
    
            She also claims she gifted Derrick's children -- Chadwick's nephews -- approximately $300K of her own funds ... saying she did it because she knew he wanted his family taken care of after he passed.
      
    
            Taylor's asking to remain on as the estate administrator ... though, if she's removed, she also makes it clear she does not think Rubin should be appointed -- claiming there are "serious allegations" against him in other cases, which she admits she does not know to be true but thinks should at least be considered and possibly investigated before appointing him administrator here.
      
    
            Bottom line ... Taylor says she's done everything asked of her as the administrator and should not be removed from the position -- and she's willing to go to court to prove it.

'Alias' Star Kevin Weisman
                          My Ex Said My Kid Was Like Ted Bundy
                          ... Compared Her To Hamas
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 24, 2026
                            2:00 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Kevin Weisman says his ex-girlfriend, Friday Chamberlain, is refusing to leave his home and is being verbally abusive to his 18-year-old daughter ... claiming his ex compared his kid to Ted Bundy and Hamas.
      
    
            The "Alias" star made the explosive claims in court as he sought a temporary restraining order against his ex.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            In the docs, obtained by TMZ, Kevin claims Friday called his daughter a "selfish, evil demon child" and compared her to the infamous serial killer.
      
    
            Kevin said Friday told him his daughter's visits to the home "could teach Hamas a thing or two about psychological warfare."
      

            He said he dated Friday from 2022 to 2023 ... and he's afraid to go to his L.A. home because Friday keeps showing up and won't leave. He claims she has demanded $250K to vacate the home.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The actor said Friday ramped up her alleged attacks by messaging his coworkers on a film project with false claims that he had taken a bunch of naked videos of her without her consent.
      
    
            The court granted a temporary restraining order against Friday, requiring her to stay 100 yards away, barring her from contact, and ordering her to move out of his place pending a future hearing on the matter.

title: Milania Giudice Allegedly Had Suicidal Thoughts, Mental Breakdown Before Airport Police Call
description:
Teresa Giudice's Daughter
                          Cops Called After Milania Had Suicidal Though
body:
Teresa Giudice's Daughter
                          Cops Called After Milania Had Suicidal Thoughts
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 24, 2026
                            11:32 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 24, 2026
                                2:19 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Milania Giudice was allegedly experiencing suicidal thoughts and had recently been released from a hospital when police were called to Tampa International Airport ... according to a CAD log obtained by TMZ.
      
    
            The log specifically says police were told Milania was experiencing "suicidal thoughts/mental breakdown" and had recently been released from St. Anthony's Hospital. It also references a possible Baker Act situation, which is when an individual is taken to a facility for an involuntary mental health examination.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A spokesman for Tampa International Airport tells TMZ ... police received a call for assistance Wednesday at 2:20 PM. We're told there was no arrest, medical transport, or police report. The Sun was the first to report the news.
      

            The CAD log says the call was classified as an "Assist Person" at the United Airlines ticket counter in the airport's main terminal. One dispatch note says the "person got away" while a counselor was with an officer.
      
    
            Another note says Milania's mother had eyes on her while she was allegedly running through the terminal. Officers were also told she was heading toward long-term parking.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Milania was seen in a since-deleted video arguing with her mom, Teresa Giudice, at the airport while police officers appeared to be nearby.
      
    
            Milania repeatedly said, "This is what we do now," as Teresa told her, "I love you." Milania's sister, Gia Giudice, appeared to try to calm things down, telling Teresa, "Let her do what she wants to do." Milania then told her mom to “shut the f*** up."
      
    
            We've reached out to Teresa's reps and an attorney for Milania ... so far, no word back.
